bull.b: The expanding renewable pipeline and rising operating capacity support a larger platform for monetizing energy-intensive computing. Progress across operating, construction, development, and assessment stages provides multiple avenues for future growth in Bitcoin hosting, AI, and other high-performance workloads.

Retiring the major credit facility materially simplifies the capital structure and releases liens on Dorothy project assets. Lower principal obligations can improve financial flexibility, facilitate project development, and reduce constraints when Soluna seeks to fund its renewable-powered AI and computing pipeline.

The proposed Dorothy 3A joint venture adds a strategic partner with data-center development resources while aligning Soluna’s renewable power assets with AI and high-performance computing demand. If completed, the structure could accelerate deployment and broaden Soluna’s customer and revenue opportunity.

bear.b: Large losses alongside declining gross profit indicate that revenue growth has not yet translated into a durable economic model. Ongoing site ramp costs, repairs, financing charges, and operating expenses could continue absorbing the benefits of scale until new capacity reaches sustainable utilization and margins.

Negative operating and free cash flow means the current business is consuming capital rather than internally funding expansion. Continued cash burn increases dependence on financing and makes execution more sensitive to project timing, capital availability, and the company’s ability to convert development investments into recurring cash generation.

The decline demonstrates that proprietary mining revenue remains exposed to changing network economics, even as Soluna shifts capacity toward hosting. This volatility can make results less predictable and places greater importance on successfully scaling contracted or partner-supported computing services.
